topStories.headline: Federal Lawsuit Filed to Halt Marina Safeway Tower Over Toxic-Contamination Claims
topStories.dek: A newly formed nonprofit and four Marina residents sued San Francisco, PG&E, and developer Align Real Estate in federal court on September 11, demanding a halt to the fast-tracked 848-unit project until environmental reviews are complete.
topStories.body:
The long-threatened lawsuit over the Marina Safeway redevelopment became a reality on September 11, when the YesAND Foundation, Neighborhoods United San Francisco, and four Marina District residents filed a complaint in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California. The suit names the city of San Francisco, its Public Health and Planning departments, PG&E, developer Align Real Estate Partners, and Safeway parent company Albertsons as defendants.

At the center of the complaint is the city's decision to approve the project under Assembly Bill 2011, California's housing-streamlining law, while — according to the plaintiffs — allowing Align to bypass a full hazardous-waste assessment of the site. The Safeway property at 15 Marina Blvd. sits atop land that once housed a PG&E steam power plant; prior testing found petroleum hydrocarbons and other contaminants in soil and groundwater above applicable residential screening thresholds. A state Department of Toxic Substances Control official noted in a December 2025 email to city planners that contamination levels were roughly twice the commercial screening threshold and ten times the residential threshold.

The plaintiffs are asking the court to set aside the city's streamlined approval and order both the city and PG&E to investigate and remediate contamination before construction proceeds. San Francisco's city attorney said the office would review the complaint once formally served; developer Align countered that the project meets all state requirements.

The lawsuit arrives at a pivotal moment. San Francisco planners ruled in August that the revised project — now calling for a 22-story and an 18-story tower containing 848 apartments, including 86 affordable units, atop a rebuilt Safeway — qualifies for the AB 2011 fast-track path. District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill and Mayor Daniel Lurie have both previously opposed the project on scale and environmental grounds, but the Planning Department's determination largely closed off local discretionary review. The next significant milestone will be whether the court grants any injunctive relief before the city issues a final building permit.

topStories.headline: Fleet Week Returns October 4–12: Blue Angels Overhead, City Promises Better Transit After July 4 Failures
topStories.dek: San Francisco Fleet Week centers the Marina waterfront again this year, with the city under public pressure to fix the crowd-management failures that stranded spectators after the Fourth of July fireworks.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Fleet Week 2026 runs October 4 through 12, with the headline Blue Angels air show over the bay on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday, October 9–11, from noon to 4 p.m. The Parade of Ships is scheduled for Friday, October 9, from 11 a.m. to noon, with the reviewing stand at Marina Green. Free ship tours open to the public run October 7–12, excluding Friday the 9th.

The event arrives under unusual scrutiny this year. Mayor Daniel Lurie called the transit response to the July 4 fireworks crowd — estimated at more than 100,000 people — "unacceptable," and District 2 Supervisor Stephen Sherrill, whose district includes the Marina, convened a hearing to examine what went wrong before Fleet Week brought another large crowd to the neighborhood. SFMTA has published a transit advisory for the air-show weekend noting that streets around Marina Green — including stretches of Marina Boulevard and Lincoln Boulevard in the Presidio — will close during the show. The F Market and Wharves historic streetcars will switchback at Pier 39 on Saturday and Sunday; extra bus service will supplement the northern and eastern waterfront routes.

Free military band concerts begin October 5 and run through October 12 at venues across the city, including Ghirardelli Square, Grace Cathedral, Pier 39, and the Ferry Building. A festival at Marina Green with food, exhibitors, and a disaster-preparedness expo runs 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. on air-show days. Viewing from public waterfront areas is free; reserved Marina Green seats are available through fleetweeksf.org. Transit planners are urging the public to ride Muni, BART, or a ferry rather than driving to the Marina, where road closures and limited parking are expected.

topStories.headline: Kaiyō Returns to Cow Hollow as a Nikkei Handroll Bar, Reviving a Storied Union Street Address
topStories.dek: Founder John Park reopened 1838 Union Street on September 11 as Kaiyō Handroll Bar, bringing cart-to-table Japanese-Peruvian handrolls and DJ-fueled late nights back to the block where his original restaurant debuted in 2018.
topStories.body:
Kaiyō Handroll Bar opened September 11 at 1838 Union Street in Cow Hollow, reviving a familiar address with an entirely new format. The concept offers cart-to-table Nikkei handrolls — rolled fresh tableside by roving chefs — alongside Peruvian comfort dishes including ceviche and lomo saltado, plus a cocktail program built to carry the room well past dinner into late-night DJ sets.

The opening is a homecoming for founder John Park, whose Brick by Brick Hospitality Group first launched Kaiyō at the same Union Street storefront in 2018. Park closed the original Cow Hollow restaurant before developing Kaiyō Restaurant and Rooftop near Oracle Park. Rather than leave the neighborhood entirely, the group redesigned the space into a handroll bar — a format gaining momentum across San Francisco since the Mission District's Handroll Project opened as the city's first standalone handroll venue in 2022.

The menu centerpiece is the lomo saltado handroll, made with A5 wagyu and shoestring potatoes, anchoring a lineup built around Nikkei cuisine — the Japanese-Peruvian fusion style born from Japanese immigrants who settled in Peru in the late nineteenth century. The interior has been reworked with a lush garden patio and graphic-novel-inspired murals by artist Lisa Pisa, who illustrated a young girl's journey from Japan to Peru across the two restroom walls. General Manager Suzanne Miller-Smith said the team wants the space to serve equally a quick 30-minute dinner and guests lingering over cocktails.

Kaiyō Handroll Bar is open Tuesday through Sunday. Reservations via Resy are strongly encouraged on weekends.

events.title: Fort Mason Night Market
events.location: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture, 2 Marina Blvd, Marina District
events.description: The monthly free outdoor market returns to the historic waterfront campus with 60-plus craft vendors curated by West Coast Craft, 25-plus food trucks and a full bar from Off the Grid, and live music curated by Stern Grove Festival. All ages and leashed dogs welcome; runs until 10 p.m.
events.sourceName: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture

events.title: Muni Heritage Weekend: Free Rides on Vintage Streetcars and Buses
events.location: San Francisco Railway Museum, 77 Steuart St (Embarcadero)
events.description: SFMTA and Market Street Railway offer free rides on rare historic streetcars and vintage buses departing from the Embarcadero plaza every few minutes, with family activities, a guided photo walking tour on Sunday, and a Muni merchandise pop-up. Note: the 2 Sutter line will be rerouted around the event area both days.

events.title: Fort Mason Art 'Points of Departure': Film Screening and Panel
events.location: Bayfront Theatre, Building B, Fort Mason Center, Marina District
events.description: The first event in Fort Mason Center's new 'Points of Departure' series screens the 2021 documentary Tell Them We Were Here, which chronicles Bay Area visual artists and their connection to the region's cultural legacy, followed by a panel conversation. Free to attend; reserve a space at fortmason.org.
events.sourceName: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture

events.title: San Francisco Fleet Week 2026
events.location: Marina Green, Crissy Field, and SF Waterfront
events.description: The full week includes free military band concerts beginning October 5, free ship tours October 7–12 (not Friday the 9th), the Parade of Ships October 9 at 11 a.m. with the reviewing stand at Marina Green, and the Blue Angels air show October 9–11 noon–4 p.m. Viewing from public areas is free; reserved seats available at fleetweeksf.org. Driving to the Marina is strongly discouraged.

events.title: San Francisco Fall Show: Art, Antiques & Design Fair at Fort Mason
events.location: Festival Pavilion, Fort Mason Center, 2 Marina Blvd, Marina District
events.description: The West Coast's oldest international art and antiques fair returns to Fort Mason under the 2026 theme 'Métallique Chic,' featuring global dealers, designer vignettes, and a lecture series. The Opening Night Gala is October 14; ticketed show days run October 15–18.

moreNews.headline: The Yard Strength Training Opens Pod-Based Gym on Union Street in Cow Hollow This Month
moreNews.body: The Yard Strength Training, a reservation-based strength-training company, signed a lease for a roughly 4,300-square-foot space at 1906 Union Street in Cow Hollow and announced a September 2026 opening. The facility will feature eight to twelve dedicated squat-rack pods that individual members and independent personal trainers can reserve by the hour, plus shared conditioning equipment, kettlebells, cables, lower-body machines, cardio equipment, and a turf area. The company selected the Cow Hollow site after a multi-year search aimed at bridging its existing San Francisco and Mill Valley studios; it is The Yard's third Bay Area location.
moreNews.sourceName: Fitt Insider / The Yard Strength Training

moreNews.headline: Presidio Marked Its 250th Birthday With Free Screenings and a Documentary Premiere
moreNews.body: The Presidio of San Francisco observed the 250th anniversary of its founding — El Presidio de San Francisco was established September 17, 1776 — with public events held on that exact date this week. The Interfaith Center at Presidio Chapel hosted three free public showings of Captivating Saga of Crissy Field, an audio-visual program pairing a tone poem by composer Deon Nielsen Price with archival film footage tracing the site's history from the Ramaytush Ohlone people through the U.S. Army years and the restoration of the marsh. Separately, the Presidio Historical Association presented the premiere of Documenting Anza by Bike — filmmaker Luis Valle's account of his bicycle journey retracing Juan Bautista de Anza's 1776 expedition from Sonora, Mexico, to the Presidio — at the restored 600-seat Presidio Theatre, followed by a champagne reception.
moreNews.sourceName: Presidio of San Francisco / Presidio Historical Association

restaurants.name: A16
restaurants.description: Michelin Bib Gourmand–recognized Marina institution serving Neapolitan pizza from a wood-burning oven, regional pastas, and a James Beard Award–winning Southern Italian wine list.

restaurants.name: Lucca Delicatessen
restaurants.description: Family-owned Italian deli operating since 1929, serving hand-made ravioli, house-cured meats, and legendary Italian sandwiches on fresh-baked rolls.

restaurants.name: Greens Restaurant
restaurants.description: San Francisco landmark vegetarian restaurant operating since 1979 under the auspices of the SF Zen Center, with sweeping bay views from its Fort Mason waterfront dining room.
restaurants.address: 2 Marina Blvd, Bldg A, Fort Mason

restaurants.name: Morella
restaurants.description: The Marina's first Argentinian-Italian fusion restaurant, blending housemade pastas and sorrentinos with wood-smoked meats and empanadas in an eclectic, palm-filled dining room.

restaurants.name: Delarosa
restaurants.description: Bustling Chestnut Street spot beloved for Roman-style pizzas, craft cocktails, and a heated parklet ideal for communal all-day dining.

restaurants.name: Lobalita
restaurants.description: Walk-in cantina in the former Tipsy Pig space offering open-fire Mexican cooking, $14 cocktails, tostadas, guacamole, and a sprawling back patio; open Tuesday–Sunday from 4 p.m.

restaurants.name: Dragon Well
restaurants.description: Neighborhood Chinese restaurant on Chestnut Street since 1998, known for handmade potstickers, tea-smoked duck, and mahjong tables operating six nights a week.

restaurants.name: Viva Goa Indian Cuisine
restaurants.description: The city's only restaurant specializing in the coastal cuisine of Goa, with standout tandoori fish, prawn xacuti, and vindaloo on Lombard Street.

restaurants.name: Perry's on Union Street
restaurants.description: A Cow Hollow institution since 1969, Perry's serves classic American fare — Cobb salad, hamburgers, chops — beneath wood-paneled walls in its original blue-and-white checked-tablecloth setting.

restaurants.name: California Wine Merchant
restaurants.description: Marina wine destination since 1974 that pours 25–30 wines by the glass from small California producers and doubles as a retail shop with a regularly rotating list.

restaurants.name: Roaming Goat
restaurants.description: Intimate Cow Hollow wine bar featuring rare pours from Armenia and Georgia alongside elevated bar fare such as grilled halloumi with truffled honey.

restaurants.name: Horseshoe Tavern
restaurants.description: No-frills Marina watering hole known to regulars as 'The Shoe,' with cold beers, a jukebox, pool tables, and wall-to-wall TVs for sports viewing.

restaurants.name: Wilder
restaurants.description: Relaxed Cow Hollow neighborhood restaurant from the Proof Positive group, known for approachable New American dishes in a comfortable, unpretentious setting on Union Street.

restaurants.name: Little Original Joe's
restaurants.description: Lively Italian-American restaurant on Chestnut Street serving pizza, pasta, and parmigiana in a see-and-be-seen setting with leather booths and branded cocktails.

restaurants.name: Ristorante Parma
restaurants.description: One of the Marina's longest-standing restaurants on Steiner Street, serving hearty Southern Italian comfort food in a warm, family-run atmosphere for roughly 30 years.

restaurants.name: Ace Wasabi's Rock-N-Roll Sushi
restaurants.description: High-energy Marina sushi hotspot serving creative rolls alongside sake and Japanese-inspired cocktails, with a nightly happy hour from 5–6 p.m.

restaurants.name: SusieCakes
restaurants.description: Marina bakery specializing in from-scratch layer cakes, cupcakes, and cookies made with all-natural ingredients and European-style butter, with custom cakes available for special occasions.

hotels.name: Hotel Drisco Pacific Heights
hotels.description: An elegant, award-winning Pacific Heights boutique hotel in a restored 1903 Edwardian building, offering complimentary breakfast, evening wine service, and a free neighborhood car service.

hotels.name: Inn at the Presidio
hotels.description: The only hotel within the Presidio National Park, housed in the restored Georgian Revival Pershing Hall with 22 rooms and suites, daily breakfast buffet, and evening wine and cheese receptions by a fire pit.

hotels.name: Lodge at the Presidio
hotels.description: Restored historic Army officers' barracks within the Presidio offering sweeping views from the Golden Gate Bridge to Alcatraz, with complimentary breakfast and easy access to Presidio Tunnel Tops.

hotels.name: Hotel Del Sol
hotels.description: A retro 1950s motor lodge transformed into a colorful, playful boutique hotel in the Marina with a heated outdoor pool and complimentary continental breakfast in a sunny courtyard.

hotels.name: Pacific Heights Inn
hotels.description: Conveniently located between Cow Hollow and the Marina District, this inn offers free on-site parking and free Wi-Fi — rare amenities in San Francisco — making it practical for business and leisure travelers.

hotels.name: Cow Hollow Inn & Suites
hotels.description: Comfortable Lombard Street motel offering spacious rooms and suites in the heart of Cow Hollow, with easy access to Union Street dining and the Marina waterfront.

hotels.name: Infinity Hotel San Francisco, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
hotels.description: Contemporary Marina hotel in the Tapestry Collection by Hilton, offering stylish rooms, a fitness center, and convenient access to Chestnut Street restaurants and the Presidio.

hotels.name: Jackson Court San Francisco
hotels.description: A charming ten-room inn housed in a historic 1900 Pacific Heights townhouse, offering understated elegance and a quiet retreat steps from Fillmore Street shopping.

shops.name: Books Inc. in the Marina
shops.description: The Marina's full-service independent bookstore — part of the West's oldest independent bookselling company, founded in 1857 — with a strong children's section, author events, and curated staff picks.

shops.name: ei Home
shops.description: Chestnut Street boutique offering rare candles, fine fragrances, and thoughtfully curated gifts that are hard to find elsewhere in the city.

shops.name: San Francisco Optics by Alexander Daas
shops.description: Family-owned eyewear shop on Chestnut Street for over 45 years, offering a curated selection of luxury frames and prescription lenses.

shops.name: Cost Plus World Market
shops.type: Home goods and specialty foods store
shops.description: Large-format retailer on Marina Boulevard offering imported foods, wines, furniture, and eclectic home décor from around the world, a Marina neighborhood fixture for decades.

shops.name: Benefit Cosmetics (Union Street flagship)
shops.description: The original home of the San Francisco-born cosmetics brand, offering its full line alongside brow bar services in an intimate Union Street boutique.

shops.name: Plumpjack Wine & Spirits
shops.description: Well-stocked Cow Hollow wine shop connected to the PlumpJack Group, known for a smart selection of California wines, spirits, and knowledgeable staff.

shops.name: Fraîche
shops.description: Chestnut Street provisions shop specializing in artisan cheeses, charcuterie, imported pantry goods, and prepared foods for picnics and entertaining.

shops.name: Past Perfect Vintage
shops.description: Sprawling Union Street warehouse stocked with vintage and antique furniture, lighting, and home accessories from multiple dealers under one roof.

shops.name: Fillmore Strasse
shops.description: Upper Fillmore boutique carrying a well-edited selection of contemporary European clothing and accessories for women, anchoring the street's reputation as a shopping destination.

shops.name: Marin Country Mart – Starbucks / Crissy Field area
shops.description: The Crissy Field / Marina waterfront area anchored by healthy take-out options and small specialty grocers serving the cycling, hiking, and jogging community along the bay.

artEntertainment.name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture
artEntertainment.description: National Historic Landmark waterfront campus housing approximately 30 nonprofit arts organizations, theaters, galleries, and event spaces, with 1.5 million visitors annually.

artEntertainment.name: Palace of Fine Arts
artEntertainment.description: Bernard Maybeck's Greco-Roman rotunda and colonnaded lagoon — the last surviving structure from the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition — serves as a beloved public monument and private event space open daily.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Beautifully restored 600-seat theater within the Presidio presenting live music, dance, theatre, film, and special events in a historic park setting.

artEntertainment.name: ArtSeed at Tides Converge in The Presidio
artEntertainment.description: Presidio-based arts education nonprofit whose China Brotsky and Seed Galleries host year-round open-call exhibitions and mentorship programs open to the public on weekdays.

artEntertainment.name: Walt Disney Family Museum
artEntertainment.description: Engaging museum in the Presidio exploring the life and legacy of Walt Disney, with interactive galleries, archival film, and rotating special exhibitions in a stunning waterfront setting.

artEntertainment.name: Presidio Officers' Club / Heritage Gallery
artEntertainment.description: The oldest standing structure in San Francisco, the restored Officers' Club hosts free public exhibitions on the Presidio's multi-layered history, including Ramaytush Ohlone heritage and military eras.

artEntertainment.name: SFMOMA Artists Gallery at Fort Mason
artEntertainment.description: Nonprofit gallery at Fort Mason presenting and selling works by Bay Area artists, supporting SFMOMA's education and community programs.
artEntertainment.address: Bldg A, Fort Mason Center, Marina Blvd

artEntertainment.name: Gathering for Justice Gallery / Magic Theatre
artEntertainment.description: Fort Mason-based theater company known for world premieres and bold new American plays, operating since 1967 with an intimate mainstage and a second performance space.

gymsRecreation.name: Body Temp Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: Marina District hot yoga and mat Pilates studio open since 2012, offering heated yoga, sculpt, HIIT, Yin, and recovery classes with a community-focused atmosphere.

gymsRecreation.name: Karma Yoga SF
gymsRecreation.description: Pacific Heights yoga studio at 2219 Filbert Street offering hot power yoga, karmic flow, and hot HIIT flow classes in a dedicated heated space.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga – The Marina
gymsRecreation.description: Marina location of the national CorePower Yoga chain, offering heated power yoga, yoga sculpt, and restorative classes with a flexible drop-in and membership model.

gymsRecreation.name: Yoga Flow SF – Pacific Heights
gymsRecreation.description: Full-service yoga studio on Union Street offering classes in a wide range of styles and times, with a special $25 seven-day intro package for new students.

gymsRecreation.name: Bodyrok – Marina
gymsRecreation.description: High-intensity Lagree fitness studio using custom Megaformer machines for full-body sculpt sessions; the Marina location is one of several Bay Area outposts.

gymsRecreation.name: CORE40 – Marina
gymsRecreation.description: Marina Lagree fitness studio offering mat and reformer-style Pilates classes on the Megaformer for a challenging full-body workout.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Golf Course
gymsRecreation.description: Historic 18-hole public golf course inside the Presidio National Park, one of the most scenic and storied public courses on the West Coast with over 120 years of play.

gymsRecreation.name: Marina Green
gymsRecreation.description: Beloved bayfront park offering jogging paths, kite flying, windsurfing, picnicking, and unobstructed views of the Golden Gate Bridge and Alcatraz, with an outdoor fitness circuit near Fort Mason.
gymsRecreation.address: Marina Blvd between Buchanan and Fillmore

gymsRecreation.name: Crissy Field Center / Golden Gate Promenade
gymsRecreation.type: National park trail and recreation area
gymsRecreation.description: Restored tidal marsh and beach trail running 1.5 miles from the Marina to Fort Point beneath the Golden Gate Bridge, managed by the Golden Gate National Recreation Area.

gymsRecreation.name: Presidio Tunnel Tops
gymsRecreation.type: National park open space and playground
gymsRecreation.description: Opened in 2022 atop the Presidio's tunnels, this 14-acre park features San Francisco's largest playground, lawn areas, fire pits, food kiosks, and sweeping views of the Golden Gate Bridge.

gymsRecreation.name: Hot 8 Yoga – Marina
gymsRecreation.description: Marina outpost of the Hot 8 Yoga chain offering a full range of heated yoga classes from Power 1 to Yoga Sculpt, Yoga Barre, and restorative Yin in a consistently clean, spa-like environment.

gymsRecreation.name: Lafayette Park
gymsRecreation.description: Leafy hilltop park in Pacific Heights with tennis courts, grassy terraces, and sweeping city views, a favored spot for dog walking and informal recreation.

gymsRecreation.name: Alta Plaza Park
gymsRecreation.description: Tiered hilltop park in Pacific Heights with playground equipment, tennis courts, and panoramic views stretching from the bay to the hills, popular with families and dog owners.
